titulo: Keep secrets out of the text
lead: A key pasted into a document, a screenshot, or a request gives access to anyone who reads it, and it stays valid after the conversation ends. Separating the secret from everything else before saving the first version lets you share the folder without worry.
objetivo: create .env, .env.example, and .gitignore before the first commit, and know what to do if a key leaks.
hero_alt: A hand holding a key ring in front of a building concierge’s key board, with a safe in the background.

aprende.t: .env stores the key; .env.example shows only the names
Leaked? Replace the key at its source first
The AI needs the variable name, not the value

secoes.sub: The room list can be visible; the key cannot.

nos.detalhe: Stores variables: a name, an equal sign, and a value. It is not a safe: it is not encrypted, and anyone who opens the file can read it. So keep it only on your machine and never put it in Git.
The same names, with fake values. Anyone who gets the project can see what they need to fill in, but they do not get access to anything. Remember: anything ending in example is the example.

nos.sub: The list of what Git does not save
nos.detalhe: Each line is a pattern. .env matches the file; .env.* matches variants like .env.local; the line with ! makes an exception and puts .env.example back on the list of files to save.
.gitignore only applies to files Git has not saved yet. If .env is already in a commit, adding the line later does not remove it from the history. That is why the list comes before the first version.

secoes.legenda: The AGENTS.md rule says: "Never write keys or passwords in a text file; keep them in .env."

rolagem_fim.texto: The .env with the real value stays at home, .env.example can be shared, and .gitignore decides this before Git saves any version. Once the mailbag has left, crossing the paper off the list will not bring it back.

passos.titulo: A credential is the key to the room
passos.sub: Whoever has it can act as you
texto: A password, API key, and bot token let whoever has them act on behalf of your account, and you pay the bill.
Before sending a screenshot, check the corners of the screen: a visible password belongs to everyone who receives it.

exemplo.texto: The same screen, with the password covered before sending.

texto: To help, AI almost always only needs to know that the variable exists, like TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN.
A real value does not belong in a request, course example, or file sent to AI unless needed.

exemplo.texto: The bot token is in the TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN variable in .env.

texto: Create .gitignore before the first git commit. It does not remove anything that is already in the history.
In the next lesson, git status is the proof: .env must not appear.

passos.sub: Replace it at the source first
texto: If a key was published or pasted by mistake, the first fix is to revoke it on the site that created it and generate another. Deleting the message or line does not invalidate a copy someone has already seen.
Only then take care of the file and the history.

exemplo.texto: 1. Revoke and replace it. 2. Clear the file.

secoes.sub: In the meu-primeiro-agente folder. The key is fake, for practice.

blocos.conteudo:
cd %USERPROFILE%\projetos\meu-primeiro-agente
echo MINHA_CHAVE=teste123> .env
echo MINHA_CHAVE=preencha_localmente> .env.example
echo .env> .gitignore
echo .env.*>> .gitignore
echo !.env.example>> .gitignore
type .gitignore

- Never write keys or passwords in a text file; keep them in .env.
- If you need a key, mention the variable name, never its value.

abas.html:
C:\Users\ana\projetos\meu-primeiro-agente> type .gitignore
.env
.env.*
!.env.example

One > creates the file (or replaces its contents); two >> add a line at the end.

• Space before >: echo .env > .gitignore writes ".env " with a trailing space. Type it without a space: echo .env> .gitignore.
  • Key in AGENTS.md “so the agent knows how to use it”: anything in text can end up on GitHub.
  • .gitignore after the commit: .env stays in the old version.

secoes.titulo: Rehearse: keep the secret out of text
secoes.sub: Create the files and check the list.

missoes.explica: The practice value is in .env. A real key works the same way, and the file never leaves this machine.

missoes.pede: Create .gitignore with the line .env (with no space before >).
missoes.explica: One > creates the file. With no space before it, the line is exactly ".env".
Two >> add text at the end. The asterisk matches any ending, such as .env.local.
The exclamation mark puts the example back on the list of files to keep.
Three lines, in order. In the next lesson, git status proves that .env was left out.

secoes.fim: The list is ready before the first version. That's what the practice asks for.
secoes.legenda: Simulation: the commands are the same in your cmd.

exercicios.titulo: E9 · Keep secrets out of text
exercicios.texto: Create .env with the fake key, .env.example with the pretend value, and .gitignore with the three lines. Add the rule to AGENTS.md.
exercicios.pronto: type .gitignore shows .env, .env.* and !.env.example, and no file other than .env has the value teste123.

exercicios.texto: For each credential you use (subscription, token, key), write down on the project sheet where you can replace it.
exercicios.pronto: For each credential, you know which page lets you revoke it and create another, without having to search in a panic.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Where does an API key go in a project?
opcoes: In AGENTS.md, so the agent knows how to use it.
In the README, as a comment.
perguntas.explica: Keep the key only in .env, and put .env in .gitignore. .env.example should have only the name with a fake value.

perguntas.p: A colleague added .env to .gitignore a week after the first version. Was .env removed from the history?
opcoes: Yes, .gitignore deletes it from the history.
No: the old version still has .env in it.
Only if the file is renamed.
perguntas.explica: .gitignore applies from that point on, and only to files that haven’t been saved yet. That’s why it comes before the first commit.

perguntas.p: You accidentally pasted a real key into a group. What’s the first step?
opcoes: Revoke the key on the site that created it and generate a new one.
Ask everyone not to use it.
perguntas.explica: Deleting the message doesn’t invalidate a copy someone has already seen. Revoking the key at its source closes access; then you clean up the rest.
